calls.title: Monterey Peninsula is parked: what would turn it back on
calls.text: Under the stopping rule you set on Oct 30, the queue parks a college once two sessions in a row each move fewer than 3% of its programs to passing (6 of 197 here). Monterey Peninsula qualified: S584 moved none and S590 moved one, Global Studies AA-T 37243, on the catalog's words for transfer degrees. It stands at 184 passing, with the reread posted. Three of the records still failing need a change to the reader, and the session has written each one up: American Sign Language 39266 prints a pair of alternatives joined by an ampersand; Hospitality 41831 prints 'Any List A course not already selected', which the reader drops; Nursing 03633 prints Humanities and Ethnic Studies lines the reader does not keep. A fourth, Anthropology 32033, stays as printed, because the catalog's own total counts List C at 4 units. The queue turns the college back on when the reader learns those three shapes, when its 2027-28 catalog loads, or when you say so. If you want it read on now, as you asked for Glendale on Nov 2, write that in the note and press Mark done; the next scheduled session takes it first.
calls.if_no_reply: Monterey Peninsula stays at 184 of 197, and the queue moves to the college with the next largest gap.

answer.words: marked done on the Commons: "keep going to get everything you can and we'll handle the outliers afterward". Every Monterey Peninsula program is found, so S594 read it as his Nov 2 ruling for Glendale: the 13 failing records wait for the outlier pass after the harvest, and the sweep keeps to colleges with missing records.

calls.title: Glendale is parked: what would turn it back on
calls.text: Under the stopping rule you set on Oct 30, the queue parks a college once two sessions in a row each move fewer than 3% of its programs to passing. Glendale qualified: S526 and S527 each moved 5 of 226 (2.2%). It stands at 115 passing; 46 records sum to a different total than the catalog prints, and 65 still miss a course's units. Either of two things from you turns it back on. First, a structured export: ask Glendale's curriculum office for every active program's required courses with their units, as a spreadsheet from their curriculum system, and attach it in any Claude session. Second, a contact: name someone in Glendale's curriculum office who can say which printed totals are wrong, and the queue drafts the questions for you to send. Glendale's 2026-2027 catalog will restart it without you. When you have done one, write what you did in the note and press Mark done; the next scheduled session takes it first.

answer.words: Marked done on Program Requirements (22:55Z): "Let's keep going with Glendale and handle the discrepancies after all data is harvested." The queue unparks the college and reads on; the discrepancies wait until the harvest is complete.
